function.name: mobile_launch_app
function.description: Install (if needed) and open this repository's build on the shared test device (Android device, Android emulator or iOS simulator), and take the device lease. Call this before any other mobile_* tool. The package/bundle and artifact are the build REGISTERED on the repository's deploy target for `env` — the last one a pipeline published, not your task branch — so a screenshot right after this call alone shows the app WITHOUT a change you have not separately installed. You cannot open an arbitrary app.

env.description: Which environment's build to test (default: stage)

function.name: mobile_press_button
function.description: Press a hardware or system button on the connected device. Android only — the underlying press_keycode call has no iOS simulator equivalent.

function.name: mobile_read_ui
function.description: Read the view hierarchy of the current screen as XML — the mobile equivalent of reading the DOM. Use it to find the resource-id or label to address with the other mobile_* tools, and to assert what is on screen.

filter.description: Keep only lines containing this substring (case-insensitive). Use it on a busy screen to find one element.

function.name: mobile_release_device
function.description: Hand the shared test device back when you are done with it, so a task waiting on it can start immediately instead of waiting out the idle timeout. Call this as the last mobile step of your run.

function.name: mobile_rotate
function.description: Rotate the connected device (Android or iOS simulator), to check a layout in the other orientation.

function.name: mobile_screenshot
function.description: Take a screenshot of the connected device (Android or iOS simulator) and attach it to the result so you can see it. With attach_to_task it is also saved on the task.

attach_to_task.description: Also save the screenshot on the board task this run is working, where the human sees it among the task's attachments (default: false)

title.description: File name for the saved screenshot when attach_to_task is true, e.g. "checkout-iphone-error"

function.name: mobile_swipe
function.description: Swipe on the connected device (Android or iOS simulator) — scroll a list, dismiss a sheet, page a carousel.

direction.description: Direction the finger moves. "up" scrolls the content down the page.

distance.description: Fraction of the screen to travel, 0.1–0.9 (default: 0.6)

function.name: mobile_tap
function.description: Tap an element on the connected device (Android or iOS simulator). Address it by text, resource_id or content_desc; x/y is a fallback for canvases and maps.

resource_id.description: Android resource-id, with or without the package prefix (e.g. "login_button")

text.description: Visible label of the element, matched exactly (e.g. "Sign in")

x.description: Absolute x pixel; only with y, and only when no selector can address the target

xpath.description: XPath over the hierarchy from mobile_read_ui. Last resort — prefer the other three, they survive layout changes

y.description: Absolute y pixel; only with x

function.name: mobile_type_text
function.description: Type text into a field on the connected device (Android or iOS simulator).

resource_id.description: Android resource-id, with or without the package prefix (e.g. "login_button")

text.description: Visible label of the element, matched exactly (e.g. "Sign in")

value.description: Text to type into the field

xpath.description: XPath over the hierarchy from mobile_read_ui. Last resort — prefer the other three, they survive layout changes

function.name: mobile_unlock_device
function.description: Wake and unlock the connected device. Android only — an iOS simulator has no lock screen. The lease already unlocks an Android device, so this is only needed when the screen locked itself mid-run (a long read, a slow build) and the app is hidden behind the lock screen.

function.name: mobile_wait_for
function.description: Wait until an element appears on the connected device (Android or iOS simulator). Use it after a tap that starts a load, instead of taking a screenshot and hoping the screen has settled.

resource_id.description: Android resource-id, with or without the package prefix (e.g. "login_button")

text.description: Visible label of the element, matched exactly (e.g. "Sign in")

xpath.description: XPath over the hierarchy from mobile_read_ui. Last resort — prefer the other three, they survive layout changes
